ctf.cache.mission: A treasure is hidden in this room… but `ls` can't see it.
ctf.cache.indices: Some sheets hide under the rug.
Hidden files have a name that starts with a dot.
ctf.cache.schema:
📐 Hidden files (under the rug)
   `ls`      →  notes.txt
   `ls -a`   →  .  ..  .drapeau  notes.txt
   A name that starts with “.” is hidden. Detectives ALWAYS look with `ls -a`.
ctf.meule.mission: The treasure is lost in a log of 3,000 lines.
ctf.meule.indices: Read 3,000 lines by hand? No thanks.
Take the detective's magnifying glass: `grep` looks for a text in a file.
ctf.meule.schema:
📐 `grep`
   journal.log ─┬─ line 1    ✗
                ├─ …         ✗
                └─ line 2047 ✓ TG{…}
   The `grep` magnifying glass reads every line and keeps only the ones that match.
ctf.coffre.mission: The safe has a padlock. But it's YOUR safe…
ctf.coffre.indices: `cat coffre.txt` → access denied. Look at its padlocks (its permissions).
ctf.coffre.schema:
📐 Permissions (the padlocks)
   ----------  →  `chmod 644`  →  -rw-r--r--
   r = read, w = write, x = execute
   The owner always has the key to the padlocks of their files.
ctf.labyrinthe.mission: The treasure is at the bottom of a maze of rooms.
ctf.labyrinthe.indices: Opening every door by hand would take ages.
`find` looks for an object by its name in every room.
ctf.labyrinthe.schema:
📐 `find`
   .  ─ a ─ b ─ c ─ d ─ drapeau.txt ✓
   `find` visits ALL the rooms (the folder tree) for you.
ctf.code.mission: This message is unreadable… it wears a disguise: base64.
ctf.code.indices: `base64` is a disguise (an encoding), not a real padlock (an encryption).
The `base64` command removes the disguise with -d.
ctf.code.schema:
📐 Disguise ≠ padlock (encoding ≠ encryption)
   “TG{…}” ⇄ `base64` ⇄ “VEd7…==”
   Anyone can decode base64: it protects nothing!
ctf.miroir.indices: Every line is flipped, like in a mirror.
ctf.aiguille.mission: 40 sheets. Only one weighs exactly 42 bytes: that's the one.
ctf.aiguille.indices: Compare the weight of the files.
ctf.aiguille.schema:
📐 Size
   `ls -l`  →  -rw------- 1 u0 u0  42 fichier_17.txt
   `find -size` finds files by their weight: handy for the detective's investigation.

ep.rencontre.repaire: Where does {nom} come from? Look for its lair in every room of {terrain}.

ep.fichiers.enclos: Build me a pen: {un_dossier} called “enclos”, right here.
aide.fichiers.enclos: `mkdir` builds a new room (“make directory”: create a folder).
ep.fichiers.gamelle: Put a bowl in my pen: {un_fichier} called “gamelle”.
aide.fichiers.gamelle: `touch` puts down a blank sheet (an empty file). The / separates the room from the sheet.
ep.fichiers.doudou: Make a photocopy of my doudou.txt (my cuddly toy) in the pen (I want to keep it here too).
aide.fichiers.doudou: `cp` makes a photocopy: first the sheet to copy, then the room to put it in. The original stays put.
ep.fichiers.renomme: Change the label of vieux_nom.txt: put my name in lowercase, {nom_min}.txt
aide.fichiers.renomme: `mv` carries a sheet somewhere else; if it stays in the same room, it just changes its label (its name).
epa.fichiers.archive: Pack my whole pen into a suitcase: the archive “enclos.tar.gz”.
aide.fichiers.archive: `tar` packs a whole room into one tightly squashed suitcase (an archive): c = create, z = squash (compress), f = name of the suitcase.
ep.reseau.ping: Shout “Ahoy!” at your own house (localhost) and listen for the echo.
aide.reseau.ping: `ping` shouts “Ahoy!” at a house and waits for the echo. localhost = your own house. -c 3 = shout 3 times, then stop.
ep.reseau.hote: What is your house called on the network?
aide.reseau.hote: `hostname` tells the name of your house on the network.
aide.reseau.ip: Every house plugged into the network has an address, like a postal address: {ip}. `ip a` shows them all.
ep.processus.ps: Show me who is awake in the house: every {processus}.
aidea.processus.ps: `ps` shows who is awake: every {processus}. `ps -A` shows them all, even the other residents'.
ep.processus.heure: What time is it? Look at the house clock.
ep.memoire.place: How much room is left in {disque}?
aide.memoire.place: `df` shows the free room in {disque}; -h writes sizes for humans (GB, MB).
aide.memoire.ram: free shows {ram}: a big worktop where programs put their things. -h = readable sizes.
ep.memoire.poids: How heavy is my nest, with everything inside?
aide.memoire.poids: du weighs a room and everything in it; -s = just the total, -h = readable size.
ep.memoire.sac: I hid some things in my bag sac/. How many? Answer me with `echo`.
aide.memoire.sac: `ls sac` looks into the bag. The | is a pipe: it pours the list into `wc -l`, which counts the lines. Then say the number with `echo`.
ep.securite.cage: Make me a cage: {un_fichier} called “cage” in my pen.
aide.securite.cage: `touch` puts down a blank sheet (build the pen first with `mkdir` if it's missing).
ep.securite.cachette: Hide a secret in my pen: {un_fichier} whose name starts with a dot.
aide.securite.cachette: A sheet whose name starts with a dot hides under the rug: `ls` doesn't see it, `ls -a` does.
ep.securite.prive: Put a padlock on my cage: nobody but you may touch it.
aide.securite.prive: `chmod` puts on a padlock (it changes the permissions). 600 = only you can read and write, nobody else.
ep.securite.empreinte: Give me the fingerprint of collier.txt (its first 8 characters, with `echo`).
aide.securite.empreinte: `sha256sum` takes a sheet's fingerprint: a string of letters and digits that changes if a single letter changes. Copy the first 8 with `echo`.
aide.code.chant: `echo` says a text. The funnel > pours it into a sheet instead of the screen.
ep.code.script: Write me a little recipe tour.sh that does an echo, then {rendre_executable}.
aide.code.script: A recipe (a script) is a sheet of commands. Write it, then `chmod +x` allows it to cook on its own: it becomes {executable} (you run it with `./tour.sh`).
ep.code.compte: Write the numbers 1 to 5, one per line, in compte.txt (with a loop!).
aide.code.compte: A for loop repeats a command for each number. Everything said falls into the sheet thanks to the funnel >.
ep.materiel.machine: What kind of house is this? Look at {processeur}.
aide.materiel.machine: `uname -m` tells what kind of brain the house has: {processeur} (x86_64, arm64…).
ep.materiel.coeurs: How many cores does {processeur} have? Answer with `echo`.
aide.materiel.coeurs: `nproc` counts the cores of {processeur}: how many things it does at the same time. Then answer with `echo`.
aidea.materiel.disques: `df` shows {disque} and their shelves (the partitions), with the space of each one.
ep.bugs.erreurs: Find the ERROR lines in bug.log.
aide.bugs.erreurs: `grep` is the detective's magnifying glass: it shows the lines that contain the word.
ep.bugs.combien: How many errors are there in bug.log? Answer with `echo`.
aide.bugs.combien: `grep -c` counts the lines found by the magnifying glass, instead of showing them.
ep.bugs.corrige: Make me a corrige.log with all the lines EXCEPT the errors.
aide.bugs.corrige: `grep -v` does the opposite: it keeps the lines WITHOUT the word; the funnel > pours them into a new sheet.
ep.nuage.photos: Put three photos in it (photo1.jpg, photo2.jpg, photo3.jpg).
aide.nuage.photos: `touch` can put down several sheets at once: write their names one after another.
ep.nuage.copie: Make a photocopy of the whole cloud in “nuage_copie”.
aide.nuage.copie: `cp -r` photocopies a whole room, with everything in it (r = recursive).
ep.donnees.debut: Just read me the top of croquettes.txt.
aide.donnees.debut: `head` reads only the top of the sheet (10 lines).
ep.donnees.lignes: How many lines in croquettes.txt? Answer with `echo`.
aide.donnees.lignes: `wc -l` counts the lines of a sheet. Then answer with `echo`.
ep.donnees.trie: Put croquettes.txt in order, into {un_fichier} trie.txt.
aide.donnees.trie: sort puts the lines in order like a dictionary; the funnel > pours the result into a sheet.
ep.donnees.differentes: How many different kinds of kibble? Answer with `echo`.
aide.donnees.differentes: sort sorts, `uniq` removes twins that follow each other, `wc -l` counts. The pipes | connect them one after another.
ep.crypto.decode: Decode message.b64 and tell me the secret word with `echo`.
aide.crypto.decode: base64 disguises a text as strange letters (it encodes it). `base64 -d` takes the disguise off (d = decode).
ep.ia.bonjour: Say hello to me with my name (with `echo`).
aide.ia.bonjour: `echo` says the text you give it.
ep.ia.chat: How many lines contain “chat” in croquettes.txt? Answer with `echo`.
aide.ia.chat: `grep -c` counts the lines where the magnifying glass finds the word.
ep.ia.frequent: What is the most frequent word in croquettes.txt? Answer with `echo`.
aide.ia.frequent: sort sorts, `uniq -c` counts each word, then `sort -n` sorts by number: the last one is the champion.
aide.retro.calendrier: cal shows the calendar hanging in the kitchen.
ep.retro.record: What is the best score in scores.txt? Answer with `echo`.
aide.retro.record: `sort -n` puts numbers from smallest to biggest; `tail -1` keeps the last one (the biggest).
ep.retro.top3: Write the 3 best scores, from biggest to smallest, in top3.txt.
aide.retro.top3: `sort -nr` sorts from biggest to smallest (r = reversed), `head -3` keeps the first 3, the funnel > pours them into the sheet.
ep.glitch.voir: Look at corrompu.txt… my words are backwards!
ep.glitch.repare: Put corrompu.txt the right way round in repare.txt.
aide.glitch.repare: `rev` flips each line, like in a mirror; the funnel > pours the result into a sheet.
ep.glitch.chuchote: I'm shouting too loud (cri.txt): write it in lowercase in chuchote.txt.
aide.glitch.chuchote: tr changes letters into other letters: here each capital (A-Z) into lowercase (a-z). The < hands it the sheet to read.
ep.systeme.qui: Who are you for the house? Ask for your resident name.
aide.systeme.qui: `whoami` (“who am I?”) tells your resident name: your username.
ep.systeme.systeme: What is the house we live in called (the system)?
aide.systeme.systeme: `uname -a` reads the house's card: its name, its version, its kind of brain.
ep.systeme.alias: Give me a command nickname, with my name, using `alias`.
aide.systeme.alias: An alias is a nickname: a short word that runs a longer command. Then type the nickname to try it!
ep.systeme.variable: Put my name in a labelled box called BESTIOLE (an environment variable).
aide.systeme.variable: An environment variable is a little box with a label that the whole terminal can open. export fills it; `echo $BESTIOLE` reads it back.

lec.t0.0.dit: Hi there! Let's visit the house together. Where is the red dot that says “you are here”?

lec.t1.2.dit: Build me a little nest in this room!

lec.t2.0.dit: I'm hungry! Take the funnel “>” and pour an apple into the box repas.txt in my nest.
lec.t2.0.bravo: Yum! Careful: the funnel empties the box before pouring. Grown-ups say “write to a file”.
lec.t2.1.dit: Read me the letter repas.txt out loud.
lec.t2.1.bravo: An apple, perfect! Grown-ups say “display a file”. Always check before you act!
lec.t2.2.dit: Grab the detective's magnifying glass: look for the word “pomme” in the letter.
lec.t2.2.bravo: The magnifying glass found it! Grown-ups say “search in a file”.

lec.t3.0.bravo: r = read, w = write, x = make it run. Grown-ups say “permissions”.
lec.t3.1.dit: Put a padlock on the box, so nobody spoils it!

lec.t4.1.bravo: Moved and renamed in one go! Grown-ups say “move” and “rename”.
lec.t4.2.dit: We don't need it anymore. Careful: this is the shredder, not the bin!

hist.reveil.debut: *knock knock*… Can you hear me? I'm very small and I'm cold. This house has been asleep for so long… Grown-ups call it "the computer". Come and find me: we'll explore it together!
hist.reveil.fin: *CRACK!* You found me! I'm not alone in the dark any more. But the house is still asleep, and I can hear monsters snoring in the rooms… First, I need a nest of my own.
hist.nid.debut: Brrr, the hallway is so draughty! Let's build a nest: {un_dossier} just for us, with a bed and a meal. Commands are our tools, like a hammer and nails.
hist.nid.fin: My nest is perfect and my tummy is full! Listen: seven wings of the house are asleep, and a family of monsters has moved into each one. You choose where to start.
hist.grenier.debut: The attic is overgrown with vines! The Sylvans pushed and mixed everything up, and my teddy bear is stuck somewhere. We need the map of the attic, then we'll tidy, copy and throw away what we don't need.
hist.grenier.fin: The attic can breathe! The vines are tidy and the Sylvans are napping on the beams. You can move, copy and throw things away like a real removal expert.
hist.cave.debut: Shh… can you hear that? The Demons in the cellar steal my food at night! To stop them, we must find out who is in charge of the house, then put {droits} on my food.
hist.cave.fin: Click, clack, padlock! The Demons tried and broke their teeth. They promised to be good… well, almost.
hist.bibliotheque.debut: Oh no, the Book of the Abyss has vanished! The Abyssals hid it between the shelves, and without it nobody can read the story of the house. Grab your magnifying glass: let's investigate.
hist.bibliotheque.fin: Book found! The Abyssals even taught us to count lines and search for words. You are a real detective of {fichiers}.
hist.machines.titre: The engine room of the Elementals
hist.machines.debut: The house can't breathe! The Elementals have blocked the pipes of the engine room. Let's check how much room is left in {ram} and in {disque}, find what's too heavy… and throw it away.
hist.machines.fin: Vrrrooom! The machines are running again and the Elementals are warming up by the boiler. The house is breathing deeply.
hist.dortoir.debut: Hoo hoo… In the dormitory, ghosts refuse to sleep! Each ghost is one {processus}, and the Undead keep waking them up. We'll count them, start one ourselves, then send them to bed.
hist.dortoir.fin: Silence… everybody is asleep. The Undead yawn and wave at us. Now you know who is awake in the house, and how to put them to bed.
hist.atelier.debut: In the workshop, the Constructs build machines that follow recipes all by themselves! We'll write {script}, make it work, give it a nickname… and take photos of our files with the magic camera, `git`.
hist.atelier.fin: Bzzt! The Constructs clap their pincers. You wrote your own commands and took your first photos of files. You're a real inventor!
hist.tour.debut: At the very top of the tower, the Celestials watch {reseau}. Our house is not alone! We'll shout "Ahoy!" to the other houses, find our address, send the postman and read the phone book.
hist.tour.fin: Ahoy, ahoy! The other houses answered! The Celestials show us the secret tunnel, `ssh`, that we'll open one day. The house is no longer alone in the world.
hist.coeur.debut: The heart of the house is beating very softly… The Aberrations scrambled everything: messages are backwards and the heart is in pieces. You'll need everything you've learned. And deep down, someone huge is sleeping: Abyssor.
hist.coeur.fin: Boom… boom… BOOM! The heart is beating! The whole house wakes up, the lights come on, and Abyssor opens one eye: "Thank you, little human." He falls back asleep, smiling. You woke up the house!
hist.telephone.debut: Behind the house there is a garden: your phone! We can switch on the torch, make it buzz, open apps… Let's go and play outside.
hist.telephone.fin: The phone garden has no secrets for you now. You control it from the keyboard, like a pro!
hist.entree.dit: Let's go! Go into the room {piece}.
hist.reveil1.0.dit: Look in your bedroom: there's an old door, terrain_terminagotchi. Push it open!
hist.reveil1.0.bravo: Creeeak… So much dust! Here we are in the great hall of the sleeping house.
hist.reveil1.1.dit: It's pitch dark. Open your eyes: what is in here?
hist.reveil1.1.bravo: A door: the hallway (vestibule). It feels like something warm is waiting for me there…
hist.reveil1.3.bravo: A warm egg! *knock knock*… It's ME! You found me!
hist.nid0.0.dit: I need a bedroom. Step back one room, into the great hall: `cd ..` means "I step back".
hist.nid0.2.dit: Put a blank sheet in the nest: it will be my bed.
hist.nid0.2.bravo: A brand-new sheet, empty and soft. Grown-ups say "create an empty {un_fichier}".
hist.grenier0.1.dit: Vines everywhere! Look at the map of the whole attic at once.
hist.grenier0.1.bravo: So many rooms inside rooms! That's {arborescence}.
hist.grenier0.2.dit: My teddy bear is stuck in the mess! Bring it back to the nest.
hist.grenier0.2.bravo: My teddy! `mv` carried it all the way to the nest. ".." means "the room next door, stepping back".
hist.t4.3.dit: Expert challenge: photocopy the whole mess at once, with all its rooms.
hist.t4.3.bravo: -r means "with everything inside" (recursive). Well done, expert!
hist.cave0.2.dit: The keeper's key is called `sudo`: it's for big jobs, not for playing. Just read its instructions.
hist.cave0.2.astuce: -h asks for no password. Never give your password to a game!
hist.cave0.2.bravo: `sudo` means "do it as {administrateur}". With it you can fix everything… or break everything. That's why it asks for a password.
hist.biblio0.1.dit: The Book of the Abyss is hidden on a shelf. Ask `find` to look for it everywhere.
hist.biblio0.1.bravo: Found it! `find` searches every room and every room inside a room.
hist.biblio0.2.dit: Open the book and read it page by page.
hist.biblio0.2.bravo: What a story! `less` turns the pages one by one.
hist.biblio1.1.dit: Read only the beginning of the book: its first 3 lines.
hist.biblio1.1.bravo: `head` reads the top of the page, like a newspaper headline.
hist.biblio1.2.dit: How many lines does this book have? Count them!
hist.biblio1.2.bravo: `wc` counts lines (-l), words (-w) and letters. Handy for a detective!
hist.biblio1.3.dit: Expert challenge: the word TRESOR is written somewhere in the library. Search all the books at once.
hist.biblio1.3.bravo: -r searches every shelf, -n gives the line number. Bravo, expert!
hist.machines0.1.dit: Listen to the house breathing: how much room is left in {ram}?
hist.machines0.1.bravo: free shows {ram}: the house's workbench. When it's full, everything slows down!
hist.machines0.2.dit: Something heavy is blocking the pipes. Weigh everything in this room.
hist.machines0.2.bravo: vieux_carton.bin is heavy! That's the culprit.
hist.machines0.3.dit: Throw away that old box (only that one, and only here!).
hist.machines0.3.bravo: Phew! The house breathes better. There's room again in {disque}.
hist.atelier0.1.dit: The Constructs left a plan on the workbench. Read it!
hist.atelier0.1.bravo: A three-step plan: write a recipe, make it work, and take a photo of everything. Let's get to work!
hist.tour2.1.dit: To get into another house, there's a secret tunnel: `ssh`. We won't open it today, just ask it who it is.
hist.tour2.1.bravo: `ssh` links two houses with an encrypted tunnel. You need the other house's key to get in.
hist.coeur0.1.dit: This message is written backwards! Turn it around with `rev`.
hist.coeur0.1.bravo: `rev` put everything the right way round: the message talks about a secret door, right here!
hist.coeur0.2.dit: A secret door? It's hidden: look even under the rug.
hist.coeur0.2.bravo: There it is: .porte_secrete! A name that starts with a dot is {cache}.
hist.coeur0.3.bravo: Brrr, it's dark… There's a piece of the heart, and someone huge sleeping.
hist.coeur1.0.dit: The heart is in three pieces, scattered around the house! Look for all the fragment files.
hist.coeur1.0.bravo: Three pieces: one here, one in the attic, one in the tower.
hist.coeur1.1.dit: Glue the three pieces into one file: `cat` reads them one after the other, > pours them into coeur_repare.txt.
hist.coeur1.1.bravo: The three pieces are together again! The heart goes "boom", very softly.
hist.coeur1.2.dit: Protect the mended heart, so the Aberrations can never scramble it again.
hist.coeur1.2.bravo: Click! The heart is under lock.
hist.coeur2.0.dit: Abyssor, the mythical guardian, talks in his sleep. Listen to what he says.
hist.coeur2.0.bravo: He wants to know how many scratches he left around the house.
hist.coeur2.1.dit: Count the files where his name is written in CAPITALS: `grep` finds, `wc -l` counts, and the pipe | passes from one to the other.
hist.coeur2.1.bravo: The pipe | plugs two commands together. Remember that number!
hist.coeur2.2.dit: Write your answer (the number, instead of the ?) in coeur/reponse.txt.
hist.coeur2.2.bravo: "That is right", rumbles Abyssor. His eyes shine like stars.
hist.lecon.finie.dit: Lesson finished! We're doing great, you and me.
hist.libre.dit: All the wings of the house are open to you! Go into whichever you like (`cd grenier`, `cd cave`, `cd tour`…) or press [a]. Type "`carte`" to see the map.
hist.aile.suite: Another wing awake ({n}/7)! Choose the next one: go into a room, or press [a].
hist.coeur.ouvert.log: 💜 The heart of the house has opened
hist.coeur.ouvert.dit: Five wings awake! I can hear something beating in the middle of the house… The heart has opened: `cd ~/terrain_terminagotchi/coeur`
hist.fin.dit: The whole house is awake, thanks to you! But a house is big: there are still lots of letters, secret rooms and quests to find. Shall we keep playing?
hist.fin.suite: Explore freely: quests (`tg quetes`), map (`tg carte`), monsters (`tg collection`).

*knock knock*
Someone in there is waiting for a friend.
hist.meuble.ours:

Its label says: "please bring back to the nest".
hist.meuble.robe: 👗 An old dress full of dust. Atishoo!
hist.meuble.jouet: 🚂 A small broken train. Maybe we'll fix it one day, in the workshop.
hist.meuble.recettes:

Apple cake: 3 apples, 1 egg, lots of love.
hist.meuble.etoiles:

At night, the Celestials count the stars from the tower.
hist.meuble.abysses: Once upon a time there was a house that fell asleep.
Demons slept in its cellar, Sylvans in its attic.
Deep down, under the heart of the house, slept Abyssor, the guardian.
He would only wake up on the day the whole house beat again.
A child and their creature would come, people said, to wake it.
They would have commands for tools, and courage for light.
The TRESOR of the house is not gold: it's the friends you find there.

hist.meuble.abyssor:
💤 Zzz… I am Abyssor, guardian of the house… Zzz…
While I slept, I left scratches everywhere.
How many files carry my name written in capitals?
Write that number in coeur/reponse.txt, and I will know you are worthy.

qu.q01.texte:
✉ Welcome letter
Welcome, little explorer! This house hides secret rooms. Their names start with a dot, so you can't see them… except with `ls -a`!
There's one right here, in the hallway. Find it and go inside (`cd`).
qu.q02.texte: 🗝 Well done, you found the secret cupboard! The old inhabitants kept their umbrellas here. There are other secret rooms in the house…
qu.q03.texte:
✉ Note from the postman
Hello! I don't know where to leave the mail. Could you build a letterbox in the hallway? A room called boite_aux_lettres will do (`mkdir`).
qu.q04.texte: 🐾 Hi, it's Pantoufle, a little Monstrous Beast! My paws are cold on these tiles. Could you put down a rug? A file tapis.txt in the hallway would be perfect (`touch`).
qu.q05.texte: 🕰 The hall clock has stopped. Ask the house what time it is and write it in vestibule/heure.txt: `date > vestibule/heure.txt`
qu.q06.texte:
🛒 Shopping list
Write at least three things to eat in nid/courses.txt, one per line. Tip: `echo apple >> nid/courses.txt` adds a line at the end.
qu.q07.texte: 🐾 I'm Grignote, the mouse of the house. Your nest looks so comfy… Will you make me a cushion? A file nid/coussin.txt will do.
qu.q08.texte: 🧸 Under the bed there are always forgotten treasures… and dust bunnies. You found a hideout!
qu.q09.texte:
📜 Grandma's recipe
Sunday cake: 2 apples, 1 smile, a pinch of patience.
Make a copy of it in your nest, just in case: `cp nid/recette_de_mamie.txt nid/recette_copie.txt`
qu.q10.texte: 📔 A diary page is waiting for you: nid/journal_intime.txt. Add a sentence about your day at the end, with >> (with a single >, you wipe everything!).
qu.q10.page:
Dear diary,
Today I found an egg.
qu.q11.texte: 🐾 Hello, I'm Mousseline the Sylvan! The vines hid my 3 socks in the attic. Bring them all back to grenier/panier/. Tip: `find grenier -name "chaussette*"` (even the hidden corners!).
qu.q12.texte: 🦉 Hoo hoo! You found the owl's secret nest, high up in the beams. It leaves you a feather as a keepsake.
qu.q13.texte:
✉ Letter from the gardener
The vines have grown leaves in grenier/lianes/. How many are there? Count them (`ls`, or `ls | wc -l`) and write the number in grenier/reponse_jardinier.txt.
qu.q14.texte: 🐾 It's Ronce! My photos are lying around in the mess. Put all the photo_*.txt into grenier/album/. Tip: `mv` moves several files at once with *.
qu.q15.texte:
📢 THEFT NOTICE
A cake has vanished! It was seen rolling towards a barrel in the cellar… Find gateau.txt (`find`) and bring it back to the nest.
qu.q16.texte: 🐾 I'm Braise, a little Demon… a nice one! I'd like a chest that nobody can damage. Create cave/coffre.txt, then put a padlock on it (`chmod 444`).
qu.q17.texte: 🕳 A trapdoor under the barrels! It's cold down here and it smells of cheese. A crystal is shining in a corner.
qu.q18.texte:
📋 Inventory to check
How many lines are there in cave/inventaire.txt? Count them with `wc -l` and write the number in cave/reponse_inventaire.txt.
qu.q18.choses: apples, pears, carrots, cheese, jam, honey, bread, nuts, milk, eggs, soup, biscuits
qu.q19.texte:
🌲 Plan of the foundations
Under the game's house lie the foundations of the whole computer: the folder /. Look at them with `ls /`… but touch nothing: these are the wild lands!
qu.q20.texte: 🐾 Bloop! It's Glouglou the Abyssal. I forgot the magic word of my aquarium! It's written in a logbook on shelf b, after "MOT MAGIQUE". Find it (`grep`) and write it in bibliotheque/mot_magique.txt.
qu.q20.journal:
Glouglou's logbook
Monday: I swam.
Tuesday: I swam again.
qu.q21.texte:
📚 Library card
The titles in bibliotheque/titres.txt are in a muddle. Put them in alphabetical order in bibliotheque/titres_ranges.txt: `sort bibliotheque/titres.txt > bibliotheque/titres_ranges.txt`
qu.q21.titres: The greedy dragon, A mouse on the moon, Zebedee the zebra, The pirates in the cupboard, My friend the robot, Goodnight ghosts, Alice and the golden key, Journey to the bottom of the sink
qu.q22.texte: 📜 The archive room! Scrolls so old they crackle when you touch them. The Abyssals hide their secrets here.
qu.q23.texte: 📖 The big book is far too long to read all of it! Read only the beginning of bibliotheque/grand_livre.txt with `head`.
qu.q23.page: Page {n}: and the story goes on…
qu.q24.texte: 🐾 Bzzt! It's Étincelle the Elemental. Are the house's cupboards full? Check the free space with `df -h`, here, in the engine room.
qu.q25.texte:
🔧 Note from the heating engineer
One of the pipes (rouge, bleu or vert) in salle_des_machines/tuyaux/ is blocked by something heavy. Weigh them with `du -sh`, then write the name of the heaviest folder in salle_des_machines/reponse_tuyau.txt.
qu.q26.texte: 🔥 The secret boiler room! This is where the chilliest Elementals sleep. It's so cosy, you could stay for hours.
qu.q27.texte: 🐾 I'm Givre, and I'm melting! Build me a fridge in the engine room (salle_des_machines/frigo) and put a glacon.txt in it.
qu.q28.texte: 🌲 A plate on the boiler says: "My real name is written in /etc/os-release". Read it with `cat` (look, don't touch: these are the wild lands).
qu.q29.texte: 🐾 Oooh… I'm a friendly Undead. I can't count the awake programs, there are too many! Count them for me: `ps aux | wc -l`
qu.q30.texte:
🕯 The night watchman's log
The night watchman wants to know the name of the head of the house. Ask `whoami` and write the answer in dortoir/veilleur.txt: `whoami > dortoir/veilleur.txt`
qu.q31.texte: 👻 Boo! Under the sheets there was… only a forgotten shooting star. The Undead use it as a night light.
qu.q32.texte: 🌙 Ghosts only fall asleep with a story. Read them dortoir/conte_du_soir.txt page by page, with `less` (q to close).
qu.q32.conte: Page {n}. The little ghost yawned, then yawned again…
qu.q33.texte: ⏰ The alarm clock wonders how long the house has been awake. Ask with `uptime`.
qu.q34.texte: 🐾 Beep! I'm Boulon the Construct. Write a recipe atelier/bonjour.`sh` that says hello (`echo 'echo Hello!' > atelier/bonjour.sh`), then run it with sh.
qu.q35.texte:
📐 Secret plan
The machine atelier/machine.sh won't start: it isn't allowed to! Make it executable (`chmod +x`), then try it: `./atelier/machine.sh`
qu.q36.texte: 🔩 Under the workbench, a hideout full of golden bolts! The Constructs keep their most precious parts here.
qu.q37.texte:
📷 Logbook
An album with only one photo is sad! Change a file in the carnet, then take a second photo: `git add`, then `git commit -m "second memory"`.
qu.q38.texte: 🐾 It's Nuage the Celestial! Did you know our house has an address all of its own, 127.0.0.1? Shout "Ahoy!" to it: `ping -c 1 127.0.0.1`
qu.q39.titre: The map of the wild lands
qu.q39.texte:
🌲 Map of the wild lands
Beyond the game's house lies the whole computer. Its name is written in /etc/hostname: read it with `cat`. Out there, we look but we touch nothing!
qu.q40.texte: 🔭 A secret observatory, at the very top of the tower! A telescope is pointed at the other houses of the internet.
qu.q41.texte:
📨 Telegram
What is the address of the house example.com? Ask the phone book (`nslookup example.com`) and write the address in tour/adresse.txt.
qu.q42.texte: 🐾 Olleh! … Sorry: hello! I'm Bizarre the Aberration, I speak backwards. Write "terminagotchi" backwards in coeur/envers.txt: `echo terminagotchi | rev > coeur/envers.txt`
qu.q43.texte: 🔊 The echo chamber… chamber… chamber… Here, everything you say comes back three times… times… times…
qu.q44.texte:
✉ Last message
How many words are in the scrambled message coeur/message_brouille.txt? Count them with `wc -w` and write the number in coeur/reponse_mots.txt.

opt.all: “all”: show everything, even the hidden objects whose name starts with a dot.
opt.long: “long”: the detailed card of each object (its padlocks, its size, its date).
opt.recursif_ls: “recursive”: also look inside every room that is inside, and inside their rooms, all the way down.
opt.recursif_cp: “recursive”: the photocopier goes into the room and copies everything inside it, along with the room itself.
opt.recursif_rm: “recursive”: the shredder goes into the room and shreds everything inside it, then the room itself.
opt.recursif_grep: “recursive”: the magnifying glass searches every letter in the room and in the rooms inside it.
opt.force: “force”: the shredder asks no questions. Careful!
opt.parents: “parents”: also builds the missing rooms along the way, and doesn't complain if the room already exists.
opt.c444: a padlock: everyone can read, nobody can write (4 = read, for you, your group, then the others).
opt.c644: a padlock: you can read and write (6 = 4 read + 2 write); the others can only read (4).
opt.c600: a padlock: only you can read and write (6); the others get nothing at all (0).
opt.c755: a padlock: you can do everything (7 = 4 read + 2 write + 1 run); the others can read and go in (5).
opt.plusx: “+” adds a right and “x” means execute: the recipe is allowed to run by itself.
opt.plusr: “+” adds a right and “r” means read: everyone can read the object.
opt.info: “Info”: the postman only brings back the envelope (the page's information), not the letter.
opt.output: “output”: the postman puts the page into the object whose name you give.
opt.human: “human”: sizes written for humans, in KB, MB, GB.
opt.summary: “summary”: a single total for the room, instead of the weight of each object.
opt.numeric: “numeric”: sort by the value of the numbers (2 before 10), not like a dictionary.
opt.name: “name”: search by name; a star stands for any piece of the name.
opt.size: “size”: search by the object's weight; c = in bytes.
opt.message: “message”: the little caption written under the photo.
opt.global: “global”: the setting counts for the whole house, not just this notebook.
opt.ignore: “ignore”: the magnifying glass makes no difference between CAPITALS and small letters.
opt.numero: “number”: the magnifying glass shows the number of each line it finds.
opt.liste: “list”: the magnifying glass only gives the names of the letters where it found the word.
opt.count: “count”: instead of showing the lines, say how many there are.
opt.count_uniq: “count”: write in front of each line how many times it comes back.
opt.inverse: “invert”: keep the lines that do NOT contain the word.
opt.nombre: “number”: how many lines to read (-n 3, or just -3: 3 lines).
opt.count_ping: “count”: shout only that many times, then stop.
opt.all_ps: “All”: all the awake programs, even those of the other residents.
opt.aux: a = from all residents, u = with the resident's name, x = even those without a terminal.
opt.tar: c = create the suitcase, z = squash it (compress), f = the suitcase's name, right after.
opt.machine: “machine”: the kind of brain the house has (x86_64, arm64…).
opt.caracteres: “c”: count the bytes (roughly, the letters and spaces).
opt.version: “version”: just say which version we have, without opening the tunnel.
opt.module: “module”: run a Python tool by its name.
opt.ecrase: the funnel: it pours the result into the object and erases what was there before.
opt.ajoute: the double funnel: it adds the result at the end of the object, without erasing anything.
opt.tuyau: the pipe: what the first command says flows into the next one.
opt.ici: here: the room you are in.
opt.avant: the room before: the one you came from, going backwards.
opt.chambre: your bedroom: your very own room (your home folder).
opt.etoile: the star: any piece of a name (photo_* = all the photo_…).
diff.rm: `rm` throws away an object · `rmdir` knocks down an EMPTY room · `rm -r` shreds a full room and everything in it (forever!).
diff.cp_mv: `cp` photocopies: the original stays where it is · `mv` moves (or renames): the original goes away.
diff.lire: `cat` reads the whole letter · `head` only the beginning · `tail` only the end · `less` page by page (q to close).
diff.touch_mkdir: `touch` puts down an empty sheet · `mkdir` builds a room.
diff.redir: `>` overwrites: the object keeps only the new text · `>>` adds at the end, without erasing anything.
diff.ls: `ls` shows the room · `ls -a` also shows the hidden objects · `ls -l` gives the card of each object.
diff.ps_kill: `ps` shows who is awake, with their number · `kill` sends a program to bed, thanks to that number.

optg.all: `-a` (`--all`): does not ignore entries whose name starts with a dot (hidden files).
optg.long: `-l`: long format: permissions, number of links, owner, group, size, modification date.
optg.recursif_ls: `-R` (`--recursive`): also lists the contents of subdirectories, recursively.
optg.recursif_cp: `-r` (`-R`, `--recursive`): copies a directory with all its contents, recursively.
optg.recursif_rm: `-r` (`-R`, `--recursive`): removes the directory and all its contents, subdirectories included; no confirmation, irreversible.
optg.recursif_grep: `-r` (`--recursive`): searches every file in the directory and its subdirectories.
optg.force: `-f` (`--force`): never asks for confirmation and ignores nonexistent files.
optg.parents: `-p` (`--parents`): creates missing parent directories; no error if the directory already exists.
optg.c444: `444`: read-only for owner, group and others (r=4, w=2, x=1).
optg.c644: `644`: read and write for the owner (4+2), read-only for group and others.
optg.c600: `600`: read and write for the owner only; no rights for group and others.
optg.c755: `755`: all rights for the owner (rwx), read and execute for group and others.
optg.plusx: `+x`: symbolic mode, adds execute permission (without u, g or o: for everyone, subject to the umask).
optg.info: `-I` (`--head`): sends a HEAD request and shows only the HTTP response headers.
optg.output: `-o` (`--output`): writes the response to the given file instead of standard output.
optg.human: `-h` (`--human-readable`; `--human` for free): sizes in readable units (K, M, G).
optg.summary: `-s` (`--summarize`): shows only a total for each argument.
optg.name: `-name`: find test on the file name, with glob patterns (`*`, `?`).
optg.size: `-size`: find test on the size; the c suffix counts in bytes (`-size 42c`).
optg.message: `-m` (`--message`): the commit message, given on the command line.
optg.global: `--global`: writes the setting to the user's configuration (~/.gitconfig), not the repository's.
optg.ignore: `-i` (`--ignore-case`): ignores the difference between upper and lower case.
optg.numero: `-n` (`--line-number`): prefixes each matching line with its number.
optg.liste: `-l` (`--files-with-matches`): only shows the names of files that contain the pattern.
optg.count: `-c` (`--count`): shows the number of matching lines instead of the lines.
optg.count_uniq: `-c` (`--count`): prefixes each line with its number of consecutive occurrences.
optg.inverse: `-v` (`--invert-match`): selects the lines that do not match.
optg.nombre: `-n` (`--lines`): number of lines to show; `-3` is the short form of `-n 3`.
optg.count_ping: `-c`: number of ICMP echo packets to send, then ping stops.
optg.aux: `aux` (BSD syntax): a = processes of all users, u = user-oriented format, x = including those without a terminal.
optg.tar: `-c` (`--create`) creates the archive, `-z` (`--gzip`) compresses it, `-f` (`--file`) gives its name.
optg.machine: `-m` (`--machine`): the name of the hardware architecture.
optg.version: `-V`: prints the SSH client version, then exits.
optg.module: `-m`: runs a Python library module as a script.
optg.ecrase: `>`: redirects standard output to a file, overwriting it (it is created if it doesn't exist).
optg.ajoute: `>>`: redirects standard output to a file, appending to the end.
optg.tuyau: `|`: pipe: the standard output of the first command becomes the standard input of the second.
optg.etoile: `*`: shell wildcard (glob): any sequence of characters in a file name.
grand.pwd: prints the absolute path of the current directory (print working directory).
grand.ls: lists the contents of a directory (list).
grand.cd: changes the current directory (change directory); a shell builtin.
grand.rmdir: removes a directory only if it is empty (remove directory).
grand.touch: creates an empty file if it doesn't exist; otherwise updates its modification time.
grand.echo: writes its arguments to standard output.
grand.cp: duplicates a file (copy): the original stays.
grand.mv: moves or renames (move): on the same file system, it is the same file (same inode) that changes name.
grand.rm: removes files (remove): no trash, it is irreversible.
grand.chmod: changes access permissions (change mode): r=4, w=2, x=1, for owner, group and others.
grand.rev: reverses the order of the characters on each line.
grand.cat: prints the contents of files, one after another (concatenate).
grand.less: paged viewer: move forward and back in a file; q to quit.
grand.head: prints the beginning of a file (10 lines by default).
grand.tail: prints the end of a file (10 lines by default).
grand.grep: prints the lines that match a pattern (regular expression).
grand.find: walks a directory tree and selects files by tests (name, size, type…).
grand.wc: counts lines, words and bytes (word count).
grand.stat: shows a file's metadata: size, permissions, inode, dates.
grand.date: prints the system date and time.
grand.ps: shows the running processes (process status), with their number (PID).
grand.htop: interactive monitor of processes and resources.
grand.kill: sends a signal to a process given by its PID (SIGTERM by default).
grand.df: used and available space on mounted file systems (disk free).
grand.du: disk space used by files and directories (disk usage).
grand.free: RAM and swap: used, free, available.
grand.uptime: time since boot, logged-in users and load average.
grand.id: the user's and their groups' identifiers (UID, GID).
grand.sudo: runs a command with another user's rights (root by default).
grand.ping: sends ICMP echo packets to check that a machine answers, and measures the delay.
grand.curl: transfers data to or from a URL (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP…).
grand.ip: shows and configures network interfaces and addresses.
grand.nslookup: queries DNS: from a domain name to an IP address.
grand.ssh: opens an encrypted session on a remote machine (Secure Shell).
grand.git: version control: keeps the history of files, commit after commit.
grand.bash: command interpreter: runs a script, or a command with -c.
grand.alias: defines a shortcut: a name that stands for a command.
grand.python3: Python 3 interpreter: runs a script, or code with -c.
grand.nano: text editor in the terminal (Ctrl+O saves, Ctrl+X quits).
grand.apt: Debian and Ubuntu package manager: installs, updates, removes software.
